body:
When close to an immersed boundary, the `column_depth` function on edges, correctly uses the `static_column_depth` equal to zero, but then picks the free surface inside the immersed boundary, which leaves a value to it. 
This PR fixes this behavior by zeroing out the `column_depth` when the static depth is zero (we are on an immersed edge)

This is actually already done in #5351 but it probably deserves its own PR (I also need it in NumericalEarth)
title: Fix column_depth when close to an immersed boundary

body:
Profiles of the kernel launching process showed that there were large overheads associated with each call. This was/is being caused by "slurping"/"splatting" the arguments between function calls, which results in allocations of Tuples for each argument.

I have gone through the launch functions to reduce this as much as possible. My idea is to have the arguments that are used for launching be explicit, i.e.:
- `arch`
- `workspec`
- `kernel!`

Then the arguments for the kernel itself are slurped at the initial call, and then passed along as a tuple to further calls as much as possible.

For single kernel launches (specifically launching `compute_hydrostatic_free_surface_Gc!`) this reduces the overhead by ~20% (360KiB to 260KiB).

labels.description: So we can get the wrong answer even faster
labels.name: performance 🏍️

labels.description: runs preconfigured benchamarks and spits out timing
labels.name: benchmark performance

title: Reduce kernel launching overhead

body:
Closes #5716. `regrid!` now composes the existing single-dimension conservative regrids when the grids differ in more than one dimension (including all three), instead of throwing. Intermediate grids are built with `constructor_arguments`, swapping one dimension at a time toward the target, so the result is exact for `RectilinearGrid` and `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` since cell volumes factorize per dimension.

- Same constraints as single-dimension `regrid!`: same grid class and topology, `Center` locations along the regridded dimensions, GPU-native.
- Also fixes #5825: `regrid_in_x!`/`regrid_in_y!` with a `Periodic` transverse dimension — the source face count was `N` instead of `N + 1`, so the last row/column lost all fractional-cell contributions (a constant field regridded to half its value there).
- Also fixes #5830: the kernels' face search probes index `N + 1`, past the end of the face array of a swept `Periodic` dimension — a silent out-of-bounds read, and a `BoundsError` under `--check-bounds=yes`. Faces now include the closing halo face.
- Tests check against brute-force cell-overlap integrals and integral conservation on both grid classes.

```julia
using Oceananigans

source_grid = RectilinearGrid(size=(4, 4, 4), x=[0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.65, 1.1], y=[0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.9, 1.4],
                              z=[-1, -0.7, -0.45, -0.2, 0], topology=(Bounded, Bounded, Bounded))
target_grid = RectilinearGrid(size=(2, 3, 2), x=(0, 1.1), y=(0, 1.4), z=(-1, 0),
                              topology=(Bounded, Bounded, Bounded))

c = CenterField(source_grid)
set!(c, (x, y, z) -> x + y * z)

regrid!(CenterField(target_grid), c)  # previously an ArgumentError
```

title: Support multi-dimensional conservative regridding with `regrid!`
